subject: [PATCH v5 10/15] NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set

2026-09-01.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance issue in the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) component of the Linux kernel. When attempting to set up listeners, the code would register each listener individually with rpcbind, which could lead to a high number of timeouts and potentially cause the system to hang. The patch introduces a check for rpcbind failures before creating new listeners, and if a failure is detected, it skips registering with rpcbind for subsequent listeners. This approach reduces the likelihood of timeouts and prevents the system from becoming unresponsive.
